summary.headline: Skipper Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,666 crore (+29.4% YoY) and PAT rose 70% to INR75.6 crore; FY27 guided to 15% revenue and ~30% PAT growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter to date: revenue INR1,666 crore (+29.4% YoY), EBITDA INR173.4 crore (+40.2%, margin 10.4% vs 9.6%) and PAT INR75.6 crore (+70%, margin 4.5%). FY26 revenue reached INR5,552.8 crore (+20%) with PAT of INR207.3 crore (+42%) and EBITDA margin of 10.3%. Order book closed at a record INR8,501.9 crore on record FY26 inflows of INR5,678 crore, but management flagged a temporary slowdown in domestic bidding and export disruption from the Middle East conflict, and guided FY27 conservatively at 15% revenue growth. Trade receivables rose sharply to INR1,485 crore, which management attributed mainly to a INR260 crore collection slipping into April and higher domestic billing.

segments.name: Engineering (T&D)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,248 crore, up over 33% YoY; FY26 revenue INR4,359 crore, up 24% YoY on transmission infrastructure demand.

segments.name: Polymer
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue crossed INR500 crore (about INR507 crore) as a record; volumes grew about 40% while value growth was lower due to lower commodity prices. Margin still low single digit.

segments.name: Infra / non-T&D
segments.commentary: Management said non-T&D is about 14% of the order book, mainly O&M for a BSNL project; infra revenue is largely T&D-driven. Order book has fallen from about INR2,000 crore to about INR1,000 crore over 6-7 quarters, per analyst.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: about 15% revenue growth (conservative, on an elevated base) and about 30% bottom-line growth, which management said is backed by the existing order book rather than new orders.
No explicit FY27 EBITDA margin number; management expects some margin improvement over FY26 but called it a challenging year with higher costs. Long-term aspiration is 12% EBITDA margin.
Management expects a return to 20-25% growth from FY28 as exports reopen and domestic bidding recovers; order awarding expected to approach FY25 levels from FY27.
FY27 capex guided at about INR250 crore, similar to prior years.
Export order book targeted to rise to 25% and eventually 50% of the order book (currently about 10%).
capex_capacity: Capacity expansion of 75,000 tonnes is due for commissioning by June 2026 (spillover from March), taking capacity to 450,000 tpa; utilisation above 85%.
Further 75,000 tpa planned in each of FY27 and FY28, targeting 600,000 tpa by FY28.
Management expects significant use of the new 75,000 tpa from Q3 FY27; full utilisation takes a couple of quarters. Expansion is expected to add about INR1,000-1,200 crore revenue annually.
Test Bed 2 commissioned, giving dual test beds at one location; a 293-tonne tower test set a record and a 350-tonne test is planned next month.
Growing substation business: about 4 high-voltage substation projects currently being executed.
demand_pricing: Order book INR8,501.9 crore (90% domestic, 10% export); FY26 inflows INR5,678 crore; Q4 inflow INR1,029 crore.
Bidding pipeline over INR33,000 crore, about 60-65% domestic and balance export; historical order conversion of 20-25%.

FY26 domestic bidding was well below FY25 because of ROW, forest clearance and transformer/HVDC equipment constraints; several projects (e.g., Krishnagiri REZ Ph-1, Vizag-Kakinada-Tuticorin, 800 kV Barmer HVDC) slipped into FY27. Management said bidding rebounded in April.

Export pressure: Middle East disruption and higher sea freight are slowing decisions in export markets; management said freight is largely passed through via FOB/CIF renegotiation and export is about 10% of the order book.
Pricing: mix of variable- and firm-price contracts; management said firm-price contracts carry buffers for commodity inflation. Raw materials are 100% indigenous.

Market share: Power Grid holds about 50% of TBCB bids and is over 90% of the domestic order book; private developers under 10%. Skipper claims about 50% of transmission-line capex as addressable (about INR50,000 crore on a INR1 lakh crore annual base).

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables almost double to INR1,485 crore despite 20% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a INR260 crore receipt due in late March came in on 1-2 April, and domestic Q4 revenue rose about 45% YoY with longer domestic realisation cycles plus GST; INR600-700 crore was already realised in April. Management said none of the debtors are sticky.

qa_highlights.question: What conversion ratio applies to the INR33,000 crore pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Historically 20-25%; management hopes to maintain that but declined to give an inflow number.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 revenue guidance only 15% if order book is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Export execution is uncertain given geopolitics and export orders are unlikely to execute this year; management called 15% conservative on an elevated base, with effort to beat it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY27 EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: No exact guidance; management expects to improve on FY26's about 50 bps gain, with long-term aim of 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company move more capacity to domestic and maintain 20% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic bidding was weak in FY26 and it is pursuing domestic opportunities, but kept guidance conservative; 20-25% growth expected from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioned for private-developer HVDC projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Private players are under 10% of the order book; management is in active talks with Tata Power, Adani and Resonia and says it is fully qualified for HVDC, currently executing a couple of HVDC projects.

qa_highlights.question: Are polymer non-Eastern market gains on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes grew about 40%, and presence has expanded outside the East, but the company is still small versus national players and remains focused on the Eastern region.

qa_highlights.question: Is the substation business margin-dilutive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said substation projects carry margins similar to the Engineering business on a project basis, though infra EPC is lower margin in general.

risks_watch: Receivables: confirm the INR260 crore April collection and the remaining receivables in the Q1 FY27 numbers.
Execution: right-of-way and forest clearance delays and transformer/HVDC equipment shortages could push project timelines.
Exports: Middle East disruption and sea freight costs may slow order decisions; export share target of 25% depends on this.
Capacity ramp: 75,000 tpa due by June 2026 and utilisation from Q3 FY27; slippage already happened once.
Margins: 30% PAT growth guidance relies on firm-price buffers absorbing commodity inflation; no EBITDA margin number was given.
Bidding: CEA's FY27 tender timing and the INR90,000-1,00,000 crore PGCIL bid pipeline must actually come through.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the multi-year runway and FY27 profit growth, but openly cautious on FY27 top-line (15%) because of export disruption, delayed domestic bidding and execution constraints. Management was evasive on specific numbers: no EBITDA margin guide, no order-inflow target, and no per-km HVDC opportunity size.
key_quotes: For FY '27, we are giving a guidance of 15% growth on revenue and approximately a 30% growth in bottom line.
So we are planning about 75,000 this year and again, 75,000 next year.
Our bidding pipeline remains strong at over INR33,000 crores, providing strong visibility for future order inflows.
And firm price contracts come with significant amounts -- sufficient buffer to take care of the commodity price increase.
